body: NEW FINDING B-93 (6 Nov 2026, docs/tasks/AUDIT-BUILT-2026-11-05.md; CORRECTED the same day: my first note said 400 MB is about four hours; it is about seven). The keeper refuses to KEEP a song it fetches itself from YouTube if that ONE file is over 45 minutes or 80 MB (keeper/keeper.py:66-68, constants; nothing in the admin changes them). It never applies to the Host's own music library (that is linked from the music server's folder, not fetched) and it is not a total: the total is this item's storage budget. So a 2 h 13 min recitation of Surat Al-Baqarah, a 3 h audiobook and a 70 min DJ mix can be played but never downloaded; the member reads 'Too long to keep.' with no Retry. 45:00 passes, 45:01 does not (`audit_people.py long`). Extend this item: the length and size limits become Host settings next to the storage budget, and the phone's sentence says what the person can do. Numbers to choose from (128 kbit/s is about 58 MB an hour): 80 MB is 1.4 hours (today), 250 MB about 4 hours, 400 MB about 7, 1 GB about 17. Disk is what is scarce, so one size limit protects it and a minutes limit protects nothing the size limit does not; the limit is a guard rail against a mislabeled huge upload, not a quota. The default is the advisor's decision (disk use for strangers), the owner's to overrule.
